tools.name: search_guidelines
tools.description:
Look a rule up in the UMR guidelines (umr4nlp/umr-guidelines, guidelines.md).

keywords: terms to look for, e.g. "aspect", "modal strength", "have-rel-role-92", ":quant",
"reentrancy". Passages with more of the keywords come first, then those whose heading has
them, then those that mention them most.
max_results: how many passages to return (at most 10).

Returns {"sections": [{"heading": the passage's place in the guidelines ("Part 3. ... > Part
3-3-1. Aspect"), "text": the passage (a section, or a part of a long one)}], "found": how
many passages matched}.

tools.name: propbank_lookup
tools.description:
Look up a lemma and every alternate of it in PropBank (at most 20 per call).

language is "en" or "zh". Returns Markdown: per lemma, every roleset with its roles and all
its examples (the sentence, then each argument; traces such as *T*-1 are PropBank's own),
or "not in PropBank". Lemmas over the limit are not looked up: the last line names them
(call again with them). There is no PropBank for another language (Uzbek): nothing.

tools.name: search_annotations
tools.description:
Find how a case is annotated: gold UMR annotations of whole sentences.

language: "zh" (Chinese) or "en" (English).
keywords: words or pieces to look for, matched anywhere in a sentence or its annotation:
words of the text (e.g. "发生", "wanted to"), concepts ("have-org-role-91", "identity-91"),
roles (":ARG1-of", ":manner"), attribute values (":aspect state"). Sentences with more of the
keywords come first.
max_results: how many gold sentences to return (at most 10).

Returns {"gold": [{"doc", "sentence_number", "sentence", "annotation"}], where annotation is
the sentence's whole annotation (words, sentence-level graph, alignment, document-level
annotation); "found": how many gold sentences matched in all}.

## remit

### remit-01 (make payment, give (perhaps for consideration))

- ARG0: agent, payer
- ARG1: theme, thing given/paid
- ARG2: recipient, person receiving payment

Example 1 (remit-v: all args): Recently , the " Duan and Duan Law Firm " remitted the claims, totaling 1.850million US dollars , to the three enterprises .
- ARG0: the " Duan& Duan Law Firm "
- ARG1: the claims , totaling 1.850 million US dollars
- ARG2: to the three enterprises
- rel: remitted

Example 2 (remit-v: passive, with theme and recipient): During checks , it discovered that some corporations and individuals made useof foreign trading companies that [*T*-28] have import and export operation rights , [*] allowing them toperform " import agent " business , used false customs documents [*] to cheat on exchange , in order [*] toget foreign exchange capital through tax evasion and smuggling , while the foreign trading companies earnedagent commission fees without any cost ; there was also some international speculative capital which[*T*-29] infiltrated regular items [*] -30 to get remitted [*-30] into the country ; or entered the domestic stockmarket for speculating , or false custom documents were purchased [*-31] [*] to purchase exchange [*] to derive profit from the exchange differences within Chinese territory .
- ARG1: [*-30]
- ARG2: into the country
- rel: remitted

Example 3 (remit-n): The third question is, whether this is not a case in which we-1 are entitled *PRO*-1 to make a remit without the consent of parties.
- ARG0: *PRO*-1
- ARGM-LVB: make
- ARGM-MNR: without the consent of parties
- rel: remit

Example 4 (remission-n): The earned credit will be posted to my transcript upon remission of payment of $50.00 per credit with a grade of “P” (Pass).
- ARG1: of payment of $50.00 per credit with a grade of "P" (Pass)
- rel: remission

## remission

### remission-02 (abate in intensity)

- ARG0: cause of remission
- ARG1: thing abating

Example 1 (remission-n: cancer): remission of breast cancer
- ARG1: of breast cancer
- rel: remission

Example 2 (remission-n: non-cancer and with the elusive arg 0!): effects of catecholamine depletion on antidepressant-induced remission of depression
- ARG0: antidepressant-induced
- ARG1: of depression
- rel: remission

## arrest

### arrest-01 (like a criminal)

- ARG0: police
- ARG1: criminal
- ARG2: crime

Example 1 (difficult syntax for crime): Since Mexican President Carlos Salinas de Gortari took office last December, special agents have arrested more than 6,000 federal employees on charges ranging from extortion to tax evasion.
- ARGM-TMP: Since Mexican President Carlos Salinas de Gortari took office last December
- ARG0: special agents
- ARG1: more than 6,000 federal employees
- ARG2: on charges ranging from extortion to tax evasion
- rel: arrested

Example 2 (NP only, all arguments): the arrest of opposition activists on the grounds of terrorism
- ARG1: of opposition activists
- ARG2: on the grounds of terrorism
- rel: arrest

Example 3 (NP only, Args 0 & 1): the arrest by West German authorities of five young West Germans, accused of stealing information from computers in the U.S. andEurope and selling it to the Soviet KGB
- ARG0: by West German authorities
- ARG1: of five young West Germans , accused of stealing information from computers in the U.S. and Europe and selling it to the Soviet KGB
- rel: arrest

Example 4 (All arguments): Information passed to Crimestoppers resulted in a milestone figure of the 100,000th arrest, following the arrest of a man by Durham Police for burglary.
- ARG1: of a man
- ARG0: by Durham Police
- ARG2: for burglary
- rel: arrest

### arrest-02 (stop)

- ARG0: causer of stopping
- ARG1: thing stopping

Example 1 (arrested development): China might stave off a crisis if it acts as forcefully as [it]*-1 did [*-1]to arrest the 1985 decline, when Beijing slammed the brakes on foreign-exchange spending and devalued the currency.
- ARG0: [*-1]
- ARG1: the 1985 decline
- ARGM-TMP: when Beijink slammed the brakes on foreign-exchange spending and devalued the currency
- rel: arrest

Example 2 (Arg 1 as "of" PP): The medication is very effective in the arrest of the disease's progress.
- ARG1: of the disease's progress
- rel: arrest

Example 3 (Arg 1 pre-relation): The patient was experiencing cardiac arrest.
- ARG1: cardiac
- rel: arrest

Example 4 (All arguments): Thus, the arrest of egg maturation by allatectomy might be due to the failure of the corpora allata to stimulate the mnc.
- ARG1: of egg maturation
- ARG0: by allectomy
- rel: arrest

## form

### form-01 (create, make)

- ARG0: creator
- ARG1: thing created
- ARG2: source
- ARG3: benefactive
- ARG4: attribute of arg1

Example 1 (just transitive): Peter Drake, biotechnology analyst for Vector Securities International, Chicago, thinks market uncertainty may encourage small companies to form more strategic alliances with big corporations.
- ARG0: small companies
- ARG1: more strategic alliances with big corporations
- rel: form

Example 2 (passive, with source): [NCNB Texas National]-1, formed *trace*-1 from the remnants of of the failed First RepublicBank Corp. of Dallas, contributed $76.9 million to NCNB's bottom line in the third quarter.
- ARG1: *trace*-1 (= NCNB Texas National)
- ARG2: from the remnants of of the failed First RepublicBank Corp. of Dallas
- rel: formed

Example 3 (nominal rel: forming): ---------------------- The forming of a market involves a process . This process may be very tortuous . At present , this market is in the process of forming .
- ARG1: of a market
- rel: forming

Example 4 (autogen1): Friday , 42 franchisees announced the formation of an association-- called A.P. Association Inc. -- to `` preserve the integrityof the Arby 's system . ''
- ARG1: of an association -- called A.P. Association Inc. -- to `` preserve the integrity of the Arby 's system
- rel: formation

Example 5 (autogen2): the formation of a holding company enabling the savings bank topursue nontraditional banking activities under a new federal law
- ARG1: of a holding company enabling the savings bank to pursue nontraditional banking activities under a new federal law
- rel: formation

Example 6 (With COM (probably not source in this case)): the formation of a national emergency unity government with Ariel Sharon 's opposition Likud Party
- ARG1: of a national emergency unity government
- ARGM-COM: with Ariel Sharon's opposition Likud Party
- rel: formation

Example 7 (args0 and 1): the formation of a new political party by James Soong
- ARG1: of a new political party
- ARG0: by James Soong
- rel: formation

Example 8 (with materials/source): Vortex formation out of two-dimensional orifices
- ARG1: Vortex
- ARG2: out of two-dimensional orifices
- rel: formation

Example 9 (swapped product/materials): Personal formation into the likeness of Christ
- ARG2: personal
- ARG1: into the likeness of Christ
- rel: formation

### form-02 (comprise)

- ARG0: components
- ARG1: whole

Example 1 (cf. 'make up'): Commission income from domestic stock and bond sales accounts form a large portion of Japanese securities companies' earnings.
- ARG0: Commission income from domestic stock and bond sales accounts
- ARG1: a large portion of Japanese securities companies' earnings
- rel: form

Example 2 (comprise again): The labels were breathy: ``Within its sheltering walls is a microcosm of a thousand years in garden design ... [a rose garden, herb garden, serpentine garden, flower fields, an apple orchard]-1 ... organized in a patchwork of 50-by-50-foot squares [*]-1 to form `rooms'...
- ARG0: [*]
- ARG1: rooms
- rel: form

# ::snt 7
# sentence level graph:
(s7r / remission-02
    :ARG1 (s7d / disease :wiki "Bone_tumor"
        :name (s7n / name :op1 "bone" :op2 "cancer")
        :mod (s7f / form)
        :mod (s7r2 / rare)
        :possessor (s7p / person :wiki "Edmond_Pope"
            :name (s7n2 / name :op1 "Pope")))
    :temporal (s7a / arrest-01
        :ARG1 s7p
        :place (s7c / country :wiki "Russia"
            :name (s7n3 / name :op1 "Russia"))
        :aspect performance)
    :aspect state)

I had no gold example of "in remission" to copy, so a few choices here are judgement calls:

- **Concept and roles:** I used PropBank `remission-02` ("abate in intensity"). Its `:ARG1` is the thing that abates, so the cancer is `:ARG1` and Pope is linked as its `:possessor`. Another reading would make Pope the `:ARG1` and attach the cancer with `:source`.
- **"a rare form of bone cancer":** In a gold example, "a form of asbestos" is annotated as `asbestos :mod (form)`. I did the same here, and added `rare` as a second `:mod`.
- **The disease:** I wrote "bone cancer" as a named `disease`, the way gold examples treat "cancer". The wiki title "Bone_tumor" is my guess.
- **Pope:** He is "Pope" here, a person probably named in full in an earlier sentence. The wiki value "Edmond_Pope" is my assumption.
- **The "when" clause:** The arrest is the remission's `:temporal`, with performance aspect (a completed past event). The remission is a state.
